walkthroughs.body_html:
Moments — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Moments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Moments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A force of 10 N acts perpendicular to a rod, 0.5 m from the pivot. Moment is:
options: 5 Nm
20 Nm

mcqs.q: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of moments about any point is:
options: zero
positive
equal to weight × distance
depends on pivot

mcqs.q: If 6 workers take 8 hours to paint a wall, how long would 12 workers take (assuming they work at the same rate)?
options: 4 hours — this is inverse proportion: double the workers, halve the time.
16 hours, because doubling the workers doubles everything including the time.
8 hours, because each worker still has to do the same job.
Sin(2x) equals sin(x)^2 by analogy with squaring.
6, by multiplying -3 by 2.
Sin(2x) equals sin(x)^2 by analogy with squaring.
9, because squaring a negative number always gives a positive.
-9 — without brackets, the exponent applies only to the 3, then the negative is applied: -(3^2) = -9.
No — sin is not a linear function; sin(2x) = 2 sin(x) cos(x).
Sin(2x) equals sin(x)^2 by analogy with squaring.
Sin is a function, so sin(2x) = 2 sin(x) by pulling the constant out.
8 hours, because each worker still has to do the same job.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Moment”?
options: Body in equilibrium if resultant force = 0 AND resultant moment about any point = 0.
For equilibrium, sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments about same point.
Beam about to tip when reaction at one support becomes zero. Useful for limit-case problems.
Turning effect of a force about a point: moment = force × perpendicular distance from pivot. Units: Nm.
